title: Enhancing Program Integrity and Interagency Coordination in the Administration of the H-1B Nonimmigrant Visa Program

enrichment.summary: This executive order directs federal agencies to work together to prevent abuse of the H-1B visa program, which is intended to bring skilled foreign workers to the U.S. but has been misused to replace American workers with lower-paid, lower-skilled foreign labor. The order requires agencies to review employer practices, coordinate on visa processing, and take actions to protect American workers and ensure the integrity of the program.
potential_concerns: The enhanced scrutiny and restrictions on employers may lead to reduced H-1B visa approvals, negatively impacting skilled foreign workers (visa-holders-work-student-tourist) seeking employment in the U.S.

Technology workers (technology-workers) who are U.S. citizens and working-age adults may benefit from greater job protections, but there is potential for slower innovation and project delays in companies heavily reliant on H-1B labor.

Large corporations (large-corporation-employees) dependent on outsourcing models may experience increased compliance costs and operational challenges due to tighter interagency coordination and wage enforcement.

The order’s focus on preventing layoffs linked to H-1B hiring might incentivize employers to delay necessary workforce adjustments, potentially disrupting the labor market and harming U.S. workers’ long-term employment prospects.
Increased enforcement efforts could lead to unintended job insecurity or exploitation risks for current H-1B visa holders if employers attempt to circumvent new policies.
